sentences: The earliest predecessors of the eye were photoreceptor proteins that sense light.
The light-sensing photoreceptor proteins that were the earliest predecessors of the eye are found even in unicellular organisms.
These early light-sensing structures are called 'eyespots'.
Eyespots can only sense ambient brightness.
Eyespots can distinguish light from dark.
Sensing ambient brightness is sufficient for photoperiodism.
Sensing ambient brightness is sufficient for daily synchronization of circadian rhythms.
Eyespots are insufficient for vision.
Eyespots cannot distinguish shapes.
Eyespots cannot determine the direction light is coming from.
Eyespots are found in nearly all major animal groups.
Eyespots are common among unicellular organisms.
Euglena is a unicellular organism with an eyespot.
The euglena's eyespot is called a stigma.
The euglena's stigma is located at its anterior end.
The euglena's stigma is a small splotch of red pigment.
The euglena's stigma shades a collection of light-sensitive crystals.
Together with the leading flagellum, the euglena's eyespot allows the organism to move in response to light.
The euglena often moves toward the light to assist in photosynthesis.
The euglena's eyespot allows the organism to predict day and night.
Predicting day and night is the primary function of circadian rhythms.
Visual pigments are located in the brains of more complex organisms.
Visual pigments are thought to have a role in synchronising spawning with lunar cycles.
Organisms could detect subtle changes in night-time illumination.
By detecting night-time illumination changes, organisms could synchronise the release of sperm and eggs.
Synchronising the release of sperm and eggs maximises the probability of fertilisation.
